title: Terraform state: the state file, remote backend and locking

videos.script: Ana applied her network, and a file appeared that she never wrote. It is called terraform.tfstate. {{file}} Inside it, every address in her configuration sits beside an id that AWS invented. That pairing is the only way Terraform knows which VPC is hers. {{mapping}} Then she cloned her own repository into a second folder and ran apply. There was no state in the clone. So Terraform built the whole network again, right beside the first one. {{duplicate}} This lesson is about that file. What it holds, how to read it, and how to change it without lying to it. {{commands}} You will watch a plan find a rule somebody added by hand, and decide which side wins. {{drift}} Then the state moves to an S3 bucket, where every laptop and every pipeline reads the same copy. {{bucket}} And because two runs can now collide, you will see a lock refuse the second one, wait for it, and outlive a process that died. {{lock}} Losing the state loses the map. The network it described is still there.
